posts.cooked:
Normally this would be about the time I announce the next meetup on Tuesday, but there was a strange message today on the Blue Moon page today. This may be simply rebranding the shop to the new name, or may be something else. TheJayMann may have more information than I, but this is the post:

 

At 11:59 PM tonight Blue Moon Games will cease operating at its current location. Don’t worry this will only result in a short disruption to the services that you have come to expect from us. Below is a list of what this means for you.

1) The awesome gamers from Indy Tabletop are stepping up and will continue to keep the doors open so that everyone will continue to have a place to play. You will not need to relocate your games to another location.

2) Blue Moon Games will not be in operation so there will be no food or retail for sale. You are allowed and encouraged to bring in outside food or beverage.

3) If you are interested in what events will be hosted be sure to check out the Indy Tabletop Facebook page or feel free to ask here.

Stay tuned for further updates on the status of the shop. All we can say at this time is that we are working to ensure that all of your gaming needs will continue to bet met for years to come and that this interruption in operations will only be temporary.

 

If anyone else has any further information, please let me know for the next regular meetup. I will pass on details once I know more. 

 

Edit: This will not actually affect the hours, but please be prepared with your own food and drinks for Tuesday. We will still be meeting at the same location at 6 on Tuesday.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
Always happy to have people come join us.

 

We're all just getting our feet wet with Pure, having only been there as a group once.

 

It's primarily a restaurant and bar. They happen to have a back area which is pretty well situated to handle a group of people playing 1 or 2 or 3 games. The tables were a bit rickety, actually, but that didn't turn out to be as annoying as I'd feared.

 

Everybody who went last time seemed to be ordering dinner. I like that I _can_ get food, but I also feel obligated to actually order something. While the prices are reasonable, they aren't super cheap, so I'm not quite sure how I feel about playing somewhere that people may feel obligated to buy things.

 

The service isn't super fast, though it also wasn't super slow. After we let the server know that people would be coming and going and ordering individually, he seemed pretty amenable to dealing with that. Hopefully the server(s) will get used to us and vice versa and things will feel smoother.

 

We had (I think) four small tables lined up in a long row and then there was at least another couple tables nearby. I think what would work better would be to have groups of two tables pushed together. I think that would make it a bit easier for people to group together into games. Probably not a big deal either way.
